components.name: Elevation source
components.desc: Connects the map to Mapterhorn's elevation tiles so that shading, colours by height, contour lines, 3D and heights can be drawn.
components.detail: `reliefInit` runs while the map is built: online it always turns relief on; offline only if at least one area was saved (else `M.rel`/`M.relDem` stay null and every relief feature is off). It loads maplibre-contour on demand (`addScript`) and creates one shared `mlcontour.DemSource` (Terrarium WebP, 512 px, zoom 0-12, decoding in a worker, cache of 24 tiles, 30 s timeout). `MH_URL`/`mhTileUrl` hold the Mapterhorn address pattern; the engine, maplibre-contour and the offline save all use the same addresses, so the offline helper can answer them from one cache.
components.netNote: online: any place; offline: only inside areas saved beforehand

mem: DemSource worker cache of up to 24 decoded 512 px DEM tiles (~1 MB each, est. ~25 MB)
store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: tile decoding in maplibre-contour's worker, off the main thread

components.name: Shading, height colours, sea depths and contour layers
components.desc: Adds the relief layers to the map: hillshade shading, colours by height, sea depths and contour lines, each switchable.
components.detail: `reliefStyle` is called by the layer builder whenever the style is rebuilt. It adds Natural Earth sea depths (`rel-bathy`, from the installed map package's `relief/bathy.pmtiles`, 5 depth bands, fading out under detailed coasts), raster-dem sources on Mapterhorn (`reldem`, plus `terrdem` for 3D terrain), a `color-relief` layer (MapLibre 5 only, checked by `engineMajor`) and a darken-only black `hillshade` whose exaggeration falls with zoom. It defines the contour source through maplibre-contour's protocol URL (thresholds per zoom in metres or feet, scaled by the reader's spacing) and three layers: thin orange lines, the 0 m coast line, and numbered labels in the font stack 'Pult'. `REL_DEF`/`relOn` give each switch's default (shading on, colours off, contours on, sea depths on) and `reliefLayerProps` returns the layers' visibility, applied without rebuilding the style.
components.netNote: tiles from Mapterhorn online, from saved areas offline; sea depths need the map package

mem: engine DEM textures for visible tiles (512 px each, est. 10-40 MB) plus contour vector tiles
store: code only; tiles cached by the engine and the offline helper
cpu: contour generation in maplibre-contour's worker as tiles arrive
gpu: hillshade and color-relief shaders over the whole map every frame

components.name: Contour spacing and numbers
components.desc: Lets the reader space contour lines closer or wider, and writes their height numbers with a font made on the device.
components.detail: `contSpacing` returns the reader's least room between lines (4-24 CSS px, default 9); `reliefStyle` scales its thresholds by it and rounds to 'nice' steps (10, 20, 25, 50 …); a change rebuilds the style after 0.5 s. For the numbers, `glyphInit` registers a `pultglyph://` protocol with MapLibre (the style's glyph URL points there). `pultGlyphs` renders only digits, comma, point, minus and space once with TinySDF from the app's 'Source Sans 3', and `pbfGlyphs` hand-encodes them as a protocol-buffer glyph file (varints, zig-zag) for range 0-255; other ranges get an empty answer. No glyph server is needed, so labels work offline.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: glyphs once; contour regeneration after a spacing change
gpu: labels drawn by the engine's symbol shader

components.name: Heights and elevation profiles
components.desc: Gives the elevation of a tapped place (on the place card) and a height profile with climb and descent for a drawn line or shape.
components.detail: `heightAt` converts a position to the Mapterhorn tile at the requested zoom (max 12), asks the shared DemSource for the decoded tile (`getDemTile`) and returns the nearest pixel's height in metres, or null without relief. `profileOf` walks a line by great-circle distance (`havKm`) and samples 121 heights at zoom 8, 10 or 11 depending on length. `profileSVG` draws them as a filled SVG curve (280 × 64) and sums total climb and descent in the map's length units.
components.netNote: offline only inside saved areas (or enlarged from coarser saved tiles)

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: up to 121 sequential tile lookups per profile

components.name: Save relief offline
components.desc: The 'Save relief offline' panel from the Globe menu: pick the detail, see the size, name the area and download its elevation tiles to the device.
components.detail: `viewArea` takes the area on screen (the whole world when the globe is wholly visible), `areaRanges`/`areaCount` list its Web-Mercator tiles for every zoom up to the chosen one (two ranges across 180°), and `mPerPx`/`fmtM`/`fmtBytes`/`areaKm`/`coordName` make that readable. `reliefSavePop`/`reliefSaveHTML`/`reliefSaveInfo` show the form (default detail: deepest zoom under 3,000 tiles; cap `RS_MAX_TILES` = 400,000) with a size estimate from five sample tiles (`areaSample`) and free storage, and a name from Nominatim (`areaName`, continents via `CONT`). `reliefSave` asks for persistent storage and runs six parallel workers over all (z, x, y): tiles already cached by another area are counted, not fetched; each fetch is retried 3 times; sizes are kept in an `x-size` header. Progress is saved every 5 s; Stop, or 50 failures, ends the job, which can be resumed later. Saving continues only while Pult is open.
components.netNote: needs Mapterhorn (tiles, size estimate) and Nominatim (name; falls back to coordinates)

store: Cache 'pult-relief': up to 400,000 WebP tiles per area - from a few MB to several GB
cpu: network-bound, six parallel requests; UI updated at most every 300 ms

components.name: Saved relief areas
components.desc: Keeps the list of saved relief areas and shows it in Settings → Maps, with Resume and Delete.
components.detail: The list (`[{id, name, w, s, e, n, z, world, total, tiles, bytes, at, state}]`) is a JSON entry `pult-relief-areas.json` in the same cache as the tiles ('pult-relief'), read once by `reliefAreas` and written by `putAreas`. `reliefAreasHTML` renders it with detail, size, date and state (saving %, incomplete %). `reliefDelete` stops a running job and deletes only tiles no remaining area covers (`areaHas`, scanning all cache keys); offline with nothing left, relief is turned off. The script's top-level listeners handle Resume/Delete clicks and the save form's detail slider and name field.

store: one small JSON entry; deleting frees relief cache space
cpu: scans every cached tile key on delete

components.name: Relief tile server (offline helper)
components.desc: Inside the offline helper, answers every Mapterhorn tile request: from saved areas first, then the network, and offline - deeper than an area was saved - by enlarging the nearest coarser saved tile.
components.detail: `reliefServe` (called by sw.js for tiles.mapterhorn.com) returns a cached tile if present, else fetches with an 8 s timeout (network-only, 30 s, for `?pult-save` requests from the downloader). Failing that, it looks up through coarser zooms for a saved ancestor and enlarges it, keeping up to 48 results in memory (`self.relMem`). `decodeDem` decodes WebP to Terrarium heights; `noisyCanvas` detects browsers that randomise canvas reads (one red step = 256 m) and then `framePixels` reads pixels through a `VideoFrame` instead. `enlargeDem` resamples the sub-square bilinearly to 512 px (smooth, not real detail), and `encodeDem` writes a Terrarium PNG with stored (uncompressed) deflate (`zlib`, Adler-32) and CRC-32 chunks (`pngChunk`, `CRC`) - compression would save ~10 % but cost 5× the time.
components.netNote: cache first, network second, enlargement when offline

mem: up to 48 enlarged tiles of ~0.8 MB (uncompressed PNG) in the service worker, plus ~1 MB float grids while enlarging (est. ~40 MB)
store: reads the relief cache
cpu: per enlarged tile: decode + 262,144 bilinear samples + PNG write, in the service worker

components.name: Map engine patches (sun shading, obelisk light)
components.desc: Changes the map engine as it loads so the relief is shaded by the real sun at every point, the night side is unshaded, and the block obelisk is lit by its own sun.
components.detail: `SHADE_PATCH` is a list of exact text replacements in MapLibre 5.24's minified code: new uniforms for the tile's longitude range and the sun (`self.__pultSun` = sin/cos of declination, subsolar longitude, on/off), per-pixel solar azimuth and altitude in the hillshade fragment shader, and a smoothstep fade around sunset. `OB_PATCH` makes fill-extrusions use `self.__pultObLight` (position, intensity) instead of the atmosphere light. `shadePatchedLib` fetches the engine script, applies each group with `enginePatch` (every search string must occur the expected number of times, else the group is skipped whole) and loads the result from a Blob URL; with another engine version it loads unchanged and shading falls back to one direction (`M.shadePatch` = false).

mem: a second copy of the engine source (~1 MB) as a Blob
store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: string replacements once at map start
gpu: a few extra shader instructions per hillshade pixel

components.name: Globe menu
components.desc: The map's 'Globe' menu: globe or flat, 3D, compass, imagery and its version, height exaggeration, elevation, shading, contour lines and spacing, Save relief, rivers and lakes.
components.detail: `mapOptsHTML` builds it from the map settings and `mapOptsPop` opens it in the right-hand popup; `mapOptsClick` handles its buttons and also the sundial's (open, Sun/Moon, Here, page swap, date style, mode, play/pause). Projection and 3D toggles animate the icon first and change the map a frame later. The icons are drawn in code: `projIconSVG` morphs a globe (`PROJ_LINES`, `projPt`, `projD`) into a Mercator rectangle, `hillIconSVG`/`chapelSVG` lift the Wurmlinger Berg's contour rings into 3D (`HILL`, `HILL_LIFT`), `iconAnim` eases between shapes over 0.45 s. `compassUpd` turns the compass needle against the map's bearing. Note: the menu sits in mapsun.js but concerns the whole map, not only relief.

store: code (~15 KB of SVG paths)
cpu: about 27 SVG rebuilds during a 0.45 s icon animation

components.name: Sun position
components.desc: Computes where the sun stands at any moment and how high and in which direction it appears from a place.
components.detail: `sunPos` uses a low-precision solar formula (days since J2000, mean anomaly, ecliptic longitude, obliquity, GMST) to give the subsolar point (declination, longitude) and the sun's ecliptic longitude (for the zodiac). `sunAt` turns that into altitude and azimuth at a longitude/latitude. Accuracy is roughly a hundredth of a degree - enough for shading and the dial.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: a few trig calls; called many times per frame by the sky

components.name: Moon position and phase
components.desc: Computes where the moon stands, which sign it is in, how much of it is lit and whether it is waxing.
components.detail: `moonPos` follows P. Schlyter's method: orbital elements, Kepler's equation solved by Newton's method, and the main longitude/latitude perturbations (about a quarter degree), then converts to the sub-lunar point and computes the illuminated fraction from the sun-moon elongation.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per dial paint and per sky frame

components.name: Night shade
components.desc: Darkens the night side of the map smoothly through twilight, as wide as it really is at each place and season.
components.detail: `sunStyle` (called by the layer builder) sets the style's light and, with sunlight on, adds a canvas source over 85° S-85° N and a raster layer `sun-night` below the region labels. `nightCanvas` makes a 512 × 256 canvas with Mercator-spaced rows; `nightPaint` fills it: each pixel's alpha follows the sine of the sun's height, smoothstepped from sunset to 18° below the horizon (max 58 % dark blue). `nightPolysAll`/`nightPolys` compute night polygons per meridian but are no longer called anywhere (dead code).

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: 131,072 pixels recomputed per sun update (every 50 ms while animating, every 30 s on Now)
gpu: one raster layer stretched over the map, texture re-uploaded per update

components.name: Sunlight on the map
components.desc: Applies the current sun to everything that depends on it: the globe's atmosphere light, the relief shading, the night shade, the dial, the obelisk and the sky.
components.detail: `sunLight` returns the style light: with sunlight on, anchored to the map and pointing from the subsolar point; otherwise from in front of the viewer. `sunApply` sets that light, publishes `self.__pultSun` for the patched hillshade shader, repaints the night canvas (playing the canvas source for two frames, then pausing), sets the hillshade direction to the sun's azimuth at the reference place (fallback when the shader patch is missing), and calls `sundialPaint`, `obelUpd` and `skyHook`.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: one full update per tick of the clock

components.name: Following the map
components.desc: Keeps the sun's reference place, the shading direction and the obelisk's shadow up to date while the map moves.
components.detail: `sunRef` decides the place whose sun is shown: the obelisk if one is set, else (dial open) the point under the dial's mark, else the map centre. `sunMove` runs at most once per animation frame on map `move`: updates the dial mark and dial, re-aims the hillshade direction if the azimuth changed by a degree, and refreshes the obelisk. `sunMoveHook` attaches it once and re-adds the obelisk and sky layer after each style load.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per frame while the map moves

components.name: Clock and animation
components.desc: Runs the sun's time: real time ('Now'), days running fast ('Animate'), the year running ('Year'), or set by hand.
components.detail: `sunOn` and `sunTime` read the switch and the current sun time (`M.sunT`). `sunClock` stops the previous timer and starts the mode: Now updates every 30 s; Animate advances time by `sunSpeed` seconds per day in a requestAnimationFrame loop and applies at most every 50 ms; Year advances whole days (keeping the hour) so a year takes `sunYear` seconds, pausing while the dial is dragged. `sunSet` saves settings and, when the sun is switched, rebuilds the map style.

store: settings in the map config (mapCfg)
cpu: while animating: a frame loop and a full sun update ~20 times a second
gpu: map repaints ~20 times a second while animating

components.name: Sundial panel
components.desc: The sundial panel at the foot of the map: a dial with sky, sea horizon, gnomon, sun and moon handle, an owl at night, and a mark showing which place it reads.
components.detail: `sdOpen` inserts or removes the panel and the triangular mark, turns sunlight on if needed and hooks map movement. `sdPanelHTML` builds the SVG: sky and sea gradients, twinkling decorative stars, 24 hour ticks, rim, stone plate, shadow line, gnomon, owl (`OWL`), sun glow and moon clipped above/below the horizon, and the zodiac wheel. `SD` holds the layout constants; `sdAng`/`sdXY` place an hour on the ring clockwise with noon at the top. `SUNDIAL_ICON` is the map button's icon.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: on open

components.name: Dial drawing
components.desc: Updates the dial to the current sun: sky colour, horizon height, the handle, the gnomon's shadow, the glitter on the sea, the moon's phase, the owl and the labels.
components.detail: `sundialPaint` computes the local sun hour, sunrise and sunset; the horizon is drawn level with sunrise/sunset on the ring (lower in summer). `skyAt` interpolates the sky gradient from `SKY_EVE`/`SKY_MORN` by the sun's height (evening red, morning rose) with `hexMix`. The shadow length follows 1/tan(altitude); the owl lands or flies off via CSS classes when day turns to night; the moon path is built from its lit fraction and waxing flag. Where the panel is at least 540 px wide it also positions and turns the zodiac wheel.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: on every sun update and map move while open

components.name: Hours and dates in three styles
components.desc: Writes the time and date under the dial in a modern, Roman or Greek manner.
components.detail: `sunHour` gives true local solar time, sunrise/sunset (with 0.833° refraction) and the sun's height. `sunLabel` shows hh:mm (modern) or, for Roman/Greek, the seasonal hour (hora I-XII / ὥρα αʹ-ιβʹ) by day and the watch (vigilia / φυλακή) by night. `sunDate` gives the local day: modern 'd Mon', Roman counting to Kalends/Nones/Ides (`romanDate`, `roNum`, `RO_MON`), or Greek as the sun's sign and degree (`grNum`, `GR_NUM`).

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per paint

components.name: Zodiac wheel
components.desc: A wheel of the twelve signs beside the dial that turns with the sun's place in the year; turning it changes the day.
components.detail: `ZOD` holds each sign's English, Latin, Greek and Greek-dative name and an SVG glyph path. `zodWheelHTML` builds the wheel (divisions, 10° ticks, glyphs anticlockwise, pointer at the top) and `zXY` places points on it. On narrow panels the wheel and the controls take turns, switched by a button showing `SWAP_ZOD` or `SWAP_DN`. Dragging the wheel (handled in the sundial's pointer listener) sets whole days by solving for the ecliptic longitude.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: on paint and drag

components.name: Sundial controls
components.desc: The controls beside the dial: Day and night switch, Now/Animate/Year, speed sliders, date style, Sun/Moon in the sky, 'Here' (obelisk) and its size, and dragging the dial to set the hour.
components.detail: `sdCtlHTML` renders the controls from the settings. `spdToV`/`spdLabel` (one day in 60 … 5 s) and `yrToV`/`yrLabel` (one year in 77 … 7 s) map logarithmic sliders. mapsun.js's top-level listeners do the work: a pointer drag on the dial sets the hour (switching to 'set' mode), on the zodiac wheel the day; `input` handlers save sky size, 3D exaggeration, contour spacing, obelisk size and speeds (debounced 0.4-0.5 s); `change` handlers switch sunlight and the Globe menu toggles.

store: settings in mapCfg
cpu: a sun update per pointer move while dragging

components.name: Reading mark
components.desc: A small triangle at the panel's top edge marks the place on the map whose sun the dial shows.
components.detail: `sdRefUpd` unprojects the screen point just above the mark to a map position and stores it as `M.sdRef`; where only sky lies there (no earth, or beyond 85°), the mark fades and the dial keeps the last place. It is hidden while an obelisk fixes the place.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per frame while the map moves

components.name: Placing and dragging the obelisk
components.desc: 'Here' sets an obelisk on the map at the next tap (and takes it away again); the obelisk can then be dragged with a finger or the mouse.
components.detail: `sunHere` toggles `mapCfg.gnomon` ({lng, lat, h}), saved with the map settings; while set, the dial, shading direction and sky use that place. `obelDragHook` catches pointer events in the capture phase before the map engine, hit-testing the 3D model's projected axis (`obel3dAxis`) or the fill-extrusion features and the foot, then moves the obelisk on every pointer move and blocks map panning meanwhile.

store: position in mapCfg
cpu: on drag

components.name: Obelisk from map blocks and its ground shadow
components.desc: Draws the obelisk with the map engine's own extruded blocks, and its shadow laid on the ground away from the sun - used when three.js is unavailable, and for the shadow on 3D terrain or long shadows on the globe.
components.detail: `obelGeo` fixes the height in metres when set (`OB_H` = 34 screen px at that zoom, times the reader's size `obelK` ⅓-3×), builds 32 stacked square extrusions (plinth, 20-step tapering shaft, 10-step point) in porphyry colours dimmed at dusk/night, and sets `self.__pultObLight` for the engine patch. The shadow is three overlapping polygons along great circles from the foot, length H/tan(altitude) capped at 8H, opacity by altitude; none at night. `obelUpd` creates/updates the `obel`/`obelsh` sources and layers (or removes them), and decides whether the three.js model draws instead; `obelShadow` refreshes after a size change.

store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per sun update

components.name: Obelisk 3D model (three.js)
components.desc: Draws a realistic red-porphyry obelisk with three.js inside the map, lit by the sun where it stands and casting a soft shadow on flat ground.
components.detail: `threeLib` imports three.js 0.169 once from `lib/` (cached by the offline helper in 'pult-lib'); on failure the map blocks stand in. `porphyryTex` paints a 256 px speckled stone texture. `obel3dLayer` is a MapLibre custom layer sharing the map's WebGL context: plinth boxes, a square frustum shaft and a pyramid point with standard materials, a directional sun light (warmer when low, dimmer at dusk) and a hemisphere sky light. It draws after the map's frame (on `render`) so it covers the atmosphere glow but is still hidden by hills; on flat ground the shadow is five stencil-masked projections from slightly shifted suns, giving soft edges.
components.netNote: three.js is fetched on first use, then cached for offline

mem: three.js module (~0.7 MB code, several MB parsed) plus a small scene and texture
store: three.js in Cache 'pult-lib' (~0.7 MB)
cpu: per map frame: matrices and a small scene render
gpu: 6 draws (×5 shadow copies) with standard materials per frame

components.name: Sky behind the map
components.desc: Paints a sky behind the globe and tilted views - Flammarion-style blue with stars, zodiac lines, the sun and the moon where they truly stand from the place shown.
components.detail: `skyHook` adds an empty custom layer `skybodies` whose render callback runs `skyDraw` every map frame; frames where view, time and settings are unchanged are skipped (v347). `skyDraw` keeps a full-size canvas `#skyBg` behind the map canvas (so the earth hides what lies behind it), fills a blue gradient, projects each sky direction 'at infinity' with the map's own camera matrix (`mat4v`, `skyDir`), turns the stars with sidereal time, and - with sunlight on - draws the sun (coloured by its height above the visible horizon, `sunSeen`) and the moon (phase, lit side towards the sun), both kept upright relative to the earth's centre. Sizes follow the setting skySize (1-24).

mem: a full-screen 2D canvas at device pixel ratio (est. 8-30 MB)
store: code only (part of the app files)
cpu: per map frame while the view or time changes: one matrix for all ~1,600 stars (a dozen multiplications each, v347); unchanged frames are skipped
gpu: a full-screen canvas composited behind the map

Both repaint the map when loaded and retry if the fetch failed.
